props.title: Beyond the Gates

sections.content: **Beyond the Gates (2016)** (2016) brilliantly taps into both VHS-era nostalgia and supernatural horror, following two brothers who discover a mysterious VCR board game in their father's video store. It's a clever evolution of horror films centered on cursed objects, like **Jumanji** (1995) and Stay Alive (2006), while capturing the vintage aesthetic that made House of the Devil (2009) so effective. The film's commitment to 1980s video store culture recalls **Video Violence** (1987) and the documentary **Adjust Your Tracking** (2013), but with a fresh supernatural twist.

sections.content: The resurgence of retro horror aesthetics has spawned several notable films mining similar nostalgic territory. **Summer of 84** (2018) captures suburban VHS-era paranoia, while **The House of the Devil** (2009) meticulously recreates 1980s horror atmosphere. **Beyond the Gates** distinguishes itself by specifically focusing on VCR board games, a unique piece of media history that existed briefly in the late 1980s and early 1990s. The film's practical effects and synthesizer score by Wojciech Golczewski cement its retro credentials.

Director Jackson Stewart draws clear inspiration from films like Phantasm (1979) and **Hellraiser** (1987), particularly in the way ordinary objects become gateways to supernatural horror. The family drama at the core - two estranged brothers dealing with their father's disappearance - gives emotional weight to the supernatural elements, similar to how The Gate (1987) used family dynamics to ground its otherworldly horror. sections.content: The film sits comfortably within the recent wave of horror examining obsolete technology, alongside films like **V/H/S** (2012), **Ring** (1998), and **Videodrome** (1983). These works share a fascination with how outdated media formats can harbor supernatural threats. **Beyond the Gates** particularly succeeds in making its VCR board game concept feel both nostalgic and threatening, much like how **Sinister** (2012) weaponized Super 8 films.
